statement: On the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of circles on the same side.
heath_proof: For, if possible, on the same straight line AB let two similar and unequal segments of circles ACB, ADB be constructed on the same side; let ACD be drawn through, and let CB, DB be joined. Then, since the segment ACB is similar to the segment ADB, and similar segments of circles are those which admit equal angles, [III. Def. 11] the angle ACB is equal to the angle ADB, the exterior to the interior: which is impossible. [I. 16]
ai_proof_text:
3.23
**Statement:** On the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of circles on the same side.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the given straight line, and suppose, if possible, that on AB two similar and unequal segments of circles, ACB and ADB, have been constructed on the same side of AB. Each segment is the figure contained by the base AB and its circumference (D3.6).

**Step 2.** Since the segments ACB and ADB are unequal, they do not coincide; for things which coincide with one another are equal (CN4). Hence the circumferences ACB and ADB are not the same circumference, and the circles of which they are parts are distinct circles. Both circles pass through the points A and B, so they cut one another at A and at B; and since a circle does not cut a circle at more points than two (3.10), the two circumferences have no common point other than A and B. Both circumferences lie on the same side of AB and have the same extremities A and B; therefore one of them falls entirely within the segment bounded by the other. Let the circumference ACB fall within the segment ADB.

**Step 3.** Take any point C on the circumference ACB other than A and B, join AC (P1), and produce AC beyond C in a straight line (P2). The point C lies within the segment ADB (Step 2). The straight line AC is distinct from AB, since C does not lie on AB; hence AC produced cannot meet AB at any point other than A. Therefore, since the boundary of segment ADB consists only of the base AB and the circumference ADB (D3.6), the produced straight line, leaving the segment ADB, must meet the circumference ADB; let it meet it at D. Thus A, C, D lie in one straight line, with C between A and D.

**Step 4.** Join CB and DB (P1).

**Step 5.** The angle ACB is the angle in the segment ACB, since C is a point on its circumference and CA, CB are joined from C to the extremities A, B of the base (D3.8). Likewise the angle ADB is the angle in the segment ADB (D3.8). Since the segment ACB is similar to the segment ADB, and similar segments of circles are those which admit equal angles (D3.11), the angle ACB is equal to the angle ADB.

**Step 6.** Now consider the triangle BCD. Its side DC, when produced beyond C, passes through A (Step 3), so the angle ACB is the exterior angle at C of triangle BCD, contained by BC and the production CA of the side DC. By 1.16, the exterior angle of a triangle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles; therefore the angle ACB is greater than the interior and opposite angle CDB. But the angle CDB is the same angle as ADB, because C lies on the straight line DA. Hence the angle ACB is greater than the angle ADB.

**Step 7.** By Step 5 the angle ACB is equal to the angle ADB, and by Step 6 the angle ACB is greater than the angle ADB. The same angle cannot be both equal to and greater than the angle ADB; this is impossible.

**Step 8.** The supposition of Step 1 therefore leads to an impossibility. Hence on the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of circles on the same side. Q.E.D.
